title: Why Cold Showers Are Good for You and the Planet
paragraphs: For many people, a hot shower is one of life's simple pleasures. However, a new study from Switzerland suggests that switching to cold showers could be good not only for your health, but also for the planet.

The study was carried out by Dr. Lena Glaser, a psychologist at the University of Basel, as part of her doctoral research. It involved 719 healthy people aged between 18 and 65 who did not normally take cold showers. For 12 weeks, they were asked to take showers that were as cold as their shower would allow. The researchers then compared them with a control group.

At first, it was not easy. Many participants dropped out during the first two weeks. After that, however, fewer people quit, which Glaser believes shows that people gradually got used to the cold water.

The participants who continued reported that they felt better both mentally and physically over time. They said that cold showers made them feel more awake and refreshed, and that they felt proud of themselves for getting through the discomfort. Even more interestingly, the participants took 31% fewer sick days than the people in the control group.

Cold showers can also help the environment, because less energy is needed to heat the water. According to the researchers, lowering the temperature of a 45-liter shower from 40°C to 15°C saves about 1.3 kilowatt-hours of energy. The participants also tended to take shorter showers, which meant they used less water. Over the 12 weeks, each participant reduced their carbon dioxide emissions by about 15 kilograms, which is roughly equal to the emissions from driving 100 kilometers. In addition, they saved money on their energy bills.

However, the study had some limitations. Some of the results were based on what participants themselves reported, and it is not known whether they continued taking cold showers after the study ended. As Glaser put it, a cold shower is not exactly pleasant, but it is a small change to make.
